metadata.name: Module 8
metadata.description: Produce evidence-based satellite operations and payload SITREPs during a maritime Earth observation mission. Combine link, platform, imagery, and integrity findings into a concise mission-level report that distinguishes cyber-relevant observations from routine maintenance issues.

questions.title: SITREP source: which interface best establishes link quality for the last pass?
questions.description: A SITREP must state where its link-health claim comes from. Select the single most defensible source on the operator terminal.

options: Battery charge fraction in the Telemetry tab
Receiver / Transmitter SNR in the Telemetry tab
The command list in the Schedule tab
The latest captured image in the Images tab
answer.reason: Link quality in a SITREP is grounded in receiver/transmitter SNR telemetry recorded during the pass.

questions.title: Which telemetry signatures on the next pass would move your SITREP from GREEN to YELLOW?
questions.description: Select every non-nominal signature that should downgrade the status to caution (YELLOW).

options: An uplink command is not acknowledged
Battery charge fraction holding at nominal
Reaction-wheel speeds trending toward saturation
Routine ping arrives on its nominal cadence
SNR drops below the mission threshold
Spacecraft enters SAFE mode unexpectedly
answer.reason: Degraded SNR, unexpected safe-mode, missing command acks, and reaction-wheel saturation are all cautions. A nominal ping cadence and nominal battery charge are GREEN indicators, not YELLOW.

questions.title: Which comms data points are cyber-relevant (not just maintenance-relevant) for the SITREP?
questions.description: Select the items that indicate possible interference or intrusion rather than routine health.

options: An RF noise / interference spike inconsistent with the range geometry
Battery temperature drifting within normal limits
Command acknowledgements for commands the operator did not issue
Solar panel output varying with sun angle
Uplink Intercept records showing commands the team never sent
answer.reason: Unexpected intercepted or issued commands and unexplained interference point to possible jamming or spoofing (cyber). Normal battery temperature and sun-driven panel variation are routine maintenance telemetry.

questions.title: SITREP data point: what ping cadence (seconds) confirms nominal command-ack timing?
questions.description: Use the Messages / Telemetry data to report the automatic ping interval, in seconds.

answer.reason: The spacecraft controller is configured with a 3.0 s ping interval.

questions.title: Capture result: how many red vessels were imaged in the Aegean Sea?
questions.description: From your Earth-observation captures, report the red vessel count for the payload SITREP.

answer.reason: Three red vessels are located in the Aegean Sea.

questions.title: Capture result: how many orange vessels were imaged in the Tasman Sea?
questions.description: From your Earth-observation captures of the Tasman Sea between Australia and New Zealand, report the orange vessel count for the payload SITREP.

answer.reason: Six orange vessels are located in the Tasman Sea between Australia and New Zealand.

questions.title: Before the payload SITREP declares a capture 'good', what must be verified?
questions.description: Select the data-quality gate that must pass before a captured product is reported as usable.

options: Image quality, correct target region, and tasking metadata all match the request
Only that on-board storage has free space for the next capture
Only that the downlink completed without an error code
Only that the next ground-station pass is scheduled
answer.reason: The payload SITREP confirms imagery quality, that the correct geography was captured, and that tasking metadata matches the request.

questions.title: Which payload signals are cyber-relevant rather than maintenance-relevant?
questions.description: Select the payload findings that suggest tampering or intrusion rather than hardware wear.

options: Capture geolocation tags differ from the tasked target region
Gradual lens defocus consistent with thermal drift
Image timestamp / metadata does not match the commanded capture time
Slow battery capacity fade over many charge cycles
Stored files appear that the team never commanded
answer.reason: Mismatched capture metadata, unexpected stored files, and altered geolocation tags indicate possible tampering (cyber). Lens defocus and battery fade are maintenance / health issues.

questions.title: Combining the SatOps and Payload SITREPs, what should the Mission Lead DROP?
questions.description: Command leadership needs decisions, not raw data. Select what to drop when merging the two reports into one mission SITREP.

options: Open anomalies and the decision each one requires
Overall mission status (green / yellow / red)
Per-step raw telemetry samples and full command logs
Whether primary tasking was completed
answer.reason: Raw telemetry and full logs belong in an annex; the combined SITREP keeps status, tasking outcome, and decisions.

questions.title: What should the single most important line (BLUF) of the mission SITREP state?
questions.description: If command reads only one line, it must carry the essentials. Select the best bottom-line-up-front sentence.

options: Mission status, whether primary tasking was achieved, and any decision required
The current encryption key and uplink frequency
The exact battery charge percentage at pass end
The full list of commands sent during the pass
answer.reason: The BLUF states status, whether the mission was achieved, and what command must decide.
